**Near and far boundaries.** Viewed from O, the near boundary is A′→S′→N′, with radial distance n(ψ) minimized at S′ (n=2√3 at ψ=30°). The far boundary is A′→T′→U′→R′, with radial distance f(ψ) maximized at U′ (|OU′|=√52 at ψ=β=arctan(3√3/5)≈46.1°).

**Swept region.** At angle φ, the swept radial set is [min n, max f] over the window ψ ∈ [φ−45°, φ] ∩ [ψ₀, 60°]. So

Area = ½ ∫ (Fmax(φ)² − Nmin(φ)²) dφ.

**Piecewise evaluation.** Splitting φ at 30°, β, 75°, β+45°, and 105°, the pieces contribute (in the integral before the ½):

- φ∈[ψ₀,30°]: 2√3
- φ∈[30°,β]: 8√3 + 2π − 12β

- φ∈[75°,β+45°]: 52(β − π/6) − 2√3

The β terms cancel, leaving 12√3 + 10π. Halving gives 6√3 + 5π.
